extracted.intended_audience: comic creators and sequential artists (graphic novelists, comic artists, webtoon creators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing comic page layouts — arranging panels, gutters, text, and white space to control pacing, reading flow, and narrative emphasis across print and digital formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control pacing, rhythm, and narrative flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Layout decisions shape every aspect of how readers experience the story: larger panels slow rhythm and invite contemplation; more panels accelerate pacing and push readers forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use panel count and size to manage reading speed; create rhythm through visual variety; strategic layout choices directly impact pacing, emphasis, and reader engagement. Example: a splash after regular grids signals importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use grid systems as structural foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Grids (4-, 6-, 9-panel or custom) provide an architectural framework from which variations can emerge while maintaining visual consistency across a narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish an underlying grid, then vary panel sizes within that framework; reserve breaks from the grid for emphasis because strategic variation is effective precisely because it’s sparing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4-panel grid
rubrics_metrics.description: Two rows of two panels (4-koma style) — simplest grid that forces efficient storytelling and steady, predictable rhythm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best for minimalist storytelling or humour where clarity matters; constraints become strengths. Example: used in The Labyrinth for philosophical clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6-panel grid
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical workhorse grid (three rows of two or two rows of three) offering versatility and steady pacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows easy panel-size variation by combining frames; balances detail and progression and serves as a default for many traditional comics.

rubrics_metrics.name: 9-panel grid
rubrics_metrics.description: Three rows of three panels popularized by Watchmen; enables precise timing and dense storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives fine control over pacing and cinematic rhythm; requires disciplined execution because clarity suffers if panels become overcrowded; breaking the grid produces dramatic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other dense/experimental grids (16+ panels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Highly dense grids appear in experimental works requiring controlled pacing and architectural complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for slow, contemplative sequences or experimental narratives (e.g., Chris Ware); panels may act as narrative containers and decorative elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thumbnailing (plan layouts before finished art)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create small rough sketches (~2 inches tall) of page layouts showing panel arrangements and text placement before committing to finished artwork.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thumbnail entire sequences to test pacing, spreads, and page turns; sketch multiple layout options for important pages; step back to test reading flow; solving problems at thumbnail stage saves major revision time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading flow: Western Z-pattern (left-to-right)
rubrics_metrics.description: Western readers follow a Z-pattern; right-side panels read as following left-side panels, and left-to-right movement appears faster and more natural.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align character movement and action with left-to-right for forward momentum; reverse movement to indicate retreat or backtracking; ensure vertical movement matches reading trajectory (e.g., descending should read down-and-right).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading flow: Manga mirror-Z pattern (right-to-left)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manga uses a mirror of Western flow: right-to-left across tiers, then down, then right-to-left again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same momentum and movement rules in mirror image; align panel sequencing and character movement with the mirror-Z to maintain natural reading dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading flow: Vertical scroll (webtoons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertical scroll eliminates horizontal reading patterns and creates flow through varied panel heights and strategic white space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use long pauses via empty space and accelerate action through rapid panel succession; lose horizontal momentum but gain fine vertical pacing control suited to mobile reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align movement with reading direction
rubrics_metrics.description: Movement across panels should match reading direction to communicate speed, forward motion, or retreat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action and pursuit: align with reading direction for momentum. Retreat/return: reverse direction to reinforce backtracking. Test layouts to ensure character trajectories don’t contradict textual description (example: Hergé’s corrections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Think in spreads for print comics
rubrics_metrics.description: Facing pages function as unified compositions; readers often view two pages at once so balance and flow must consider both pages together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design with visual balance across verso/recto, account for the central gutter splitting images, and plan how elements and movement travel across the spread for continuity and rhythm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use page turns as dramatic devices
rubrics_metrics.description: The physical page turn acts like an extended gutter and a pause in reading that can create suspense, reveal, or time jumps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place reveals or cliffhangers on the right-hand page's bottom-right (natural pause) and follow with surprise on the following page; use turns to signal narrative leaps or to maximize dramatic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel size and position create emphasis and emotional impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel scale and placement direct attention and change how moments land emotionally and narratively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger panels slow reading and invite contemplation; smaller panels quicken pace; bottom-right or right-page placement can make reveals hit harder; combine size and position deliberately to amplify beats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peeters’ layout approach: Conventional
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritizes narrative flow over page composition; steady storytelling with minimal variation within fixed frameworks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent grids to create steady reading patterns; constraints can focus attention on storytelling detail rather than spectacle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peeters’ layout approach: Decorative
rubrics_metrics.description: Treats the page as an independent aesthetic unit — prioritizes visual impact and spatial harmony potentially at the expense of sequential continuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for striking, painterly pages where each page as a unique composition matters; beware that narrative continuity can suffer if composition dominates storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peeters’ layout approach: Rhetorical
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels and pages subordinate themselves to narrative, with each compositional choice amplifying the story (classical comics approach).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place large or altered panels to mirror dramatic beats; remove borders or change structure only when it serves a clear narrative function (e.g., Eisner’s borderless memory sequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Peeters’ layout approach: Productive
rubrics_metrics.description: Page organization generates narrative possibilities; layout itself drives storytelling rather than merely serving it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for formal experimentation (e.g., McCay, Chris Ware) where page structure creates meaning; note this is hard to sustain over long works and often best at short scales or as occasional experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unclear reading order
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambiguous panel arrangements that confuse where to look next are a critical mistake in layout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow cultural reading conventions, align panel tops to reinforce tiers, use size and position to guide the eye, and test layouts with readers to catch confusion early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid monotonous layouts
rubrics_metrics.description: Repetitive identical grids drain visual energy and reduce engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary panel sizes within grids, alternate grid densities, and introduce occasional splash or large panels to restore emphasis and create visual rhythm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t ignore the spread
rubrics_metrics.description: Designing pages in isolation without considering facing-page relationships weakens compositional coherence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always view and design in spread format, balance visual weight across spreads, and plan page turns for dramatic timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always thumbnail (avoid working without thumbnails)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jumping straight to finished pages without planning leads to flow problems and expensive revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thumbnail every page and sequence, test multiple options, and resolve pacing and compositional issues in thumbnails where changes are cheap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid prefabricated panel templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Relying on generic templates treats page composition as a technical afterthought rather than narrative-driven design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design custom layouts that emerge from the story’s needs; templates can signal amateur work when convenience overrides narrative purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format considerations — print comics
rubrics_metrics.description: Print format imposes physical constraints and opportunities — spread thinking, trim size, bleed area, and central gutter affect layout choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for trim and bleed when placing images; avoid critical content lost to the central gutter; consider how page size and binding affect composition and pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format considerations — digital screen-based comics
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital display introduces different constraints and tools, including full-page display, guided view, animation, sound, and non-linear navigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design pages to work on common screen sizes, consider panel-by-panel guided view behavior, and exploit (but not overuse) digital affordances like transitions or sound to enhance narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format considerations — webtoon vertical scroll
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile-first vertical scroll removes page boundaries and controls pacing through panel height and white space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use single-column layouts, varied panel heights, and strategic white space to insert pauses or accelerate action; horizontal panels can still be used for width emphasis within vertical flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test reading flow regularly
rubrics_metrics.description: Layouts that look fine in isolation can fail when read; testing prevents errors in movement, reading order, and pacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step back from thumbnails and finished pages to follow the reading path; test with other readers to identify unclear sequences or mismatched movement.
